name: Pre-mRNA Splicing (Spliceosome Assembly)
description: Pre-mRNA splicing in S. cerevisiae removes introns via the spliceosome, a megadalton ribonucleoprotein complex. The spliceosome assembles stepwise on pre-mRNA: U1 snRNP recognizes 5' splice site, U2 snRNP binds branch point, U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP joins to form catalytic core. After extensive remodeling driven by eight DExD/H-box ATPases/helicases, two transesterification reactions occur: 2'OH at branch point attacks 5' splice site (forming lariat intermediate), then 3'OH of 5' exon attacks 3' splice site (joining exons, releasing lariat). Spliceosome then disassembles for recycling. The pathway has extremely high AND gate requirements - all snRNPs, cofactors, and catalytic rearrangements must occur in precise order. This is the paradigm for eukaryotic RNA processing complexity.
scientificAccuracy: Based on Nobel Prize-winning research on splicing mechanisms. All spliceosome components validated.
